**Finding submitted: deviation (T4C — Termination for convenience)**

**What I found**

- **Vendor side is fine.** Array has no termination-for-convenience right anywhere. Its only exits are Section 13.3 (material breach, 90/60-day cure), 13.4 (bankruptcy) and 8.2 (our Competing Product breach). That matches the preferred position.
- **Customer side fails the fallback.** Section 13.1 runs product-by-product and country-by-country until expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term — a multi-year commitment. But our at-will right in Section 13.2 only "commenc[es] on the later of" two redacted periods measured from First Commercial Sale of *both* the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products. Through the entire development and pre-launch phase we have no convenience exit at all (only 13.5 Safety/Efficacy and 13.3 breach). That is the playbook's walk-away case: no customer convenience right in a multi-year term. The notice period is also redacted, so the 60–90 day fallback band cannot be verified.

**Redline (validated ok:true)** — single minimal edit to p0628: strike the First Commercial Sale gate so the right is exercisable "at any time during the Term," in whole or on a Product-by-Product/country-by-country basis, on ninety (90) days' written notice. I used 90 rather than our preferred 30 days because the Article 14 wind-down machinery (clinical study transitions, distribution continuity, regulatory assignments) makes a short notice period genuinely impracticable here.

**Noted, not flagged twice:** the real price of a 13.2 exit sits in p0647/p0656 (we bear transfer and ongoing Clinical Study costs) and p0492 (post-termination Competing Product lock-out on an at-will exit). These are covenant/exit-cost terms rather than an early-termination fee, and belong to the exclusivity and exit-cost rules — I flagged them in the rationale instead of loading a second edit onto this clause.
